I'm 45 years old and I've been farming our family's land in Quzhou for over 20 years. I only went to primary school, so I don't read those extension pamphlets much — I watch what my neighbors do and remember what worked on my own fields. We have about 8 mu of good flat land, and every year I plant winter wheat in October and summer maize right after the wheat harvest in June. That's what everyone around here does; it keeps food on the table and if one crop has a bad year, the other usually saves us. I buy improved wheat seed from the village shop — last year I used Jimai 22 and it did fine — and hybrid maize seed, usually Denghai 605, because the yield is steadier than saving my own seed. For fertilizer, I put down about one bag of compound fertilizer per mu when I prepare the wheat field, and then I topdress with urea twice: once at green-up and again at jointing. All together that's about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu for the wheat. For the maize, the turnaround is only a few days after wheat harvest, so I don't have time for much tillage — I just plant it no-till and throw on about 12 kg of nitrogen per mu when the seedlings are knee-high. I also make sure to put phosphorus and potassium down with the compound fertilizer, about 6 kg and 5 kg per mu respectively. Water is expensive now because they meter the well, but wheat is our main crop so I irrigate it four times — winter irrigation, green-up, jointing, and filling. The maize can manage with two good irrigations, at the big trumpet leaf stage and at tasseling. I spray pesticides when I see aphids or weeds; usually about four times for wheat and three times for maize. I expect the wheat to give me around 480 kg per mu and the maize around 560 kg per mu if the weather cooperates.
